prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit plus background replacement.
Create exactly ONE finished portrait illustration by editing IMAGE 1.

INPUTS:
IMAGE 1 is the target archer artwork. Preserve its adult character, facial features, hair, rounded gold armor, hand positions, full-draw archery action, dramatic low camera, torso twist, large foreground leg and small folded rear leg. Restrict character changes to the clothing issues below.
IMAGE 2 is ONLY a reference for the inclined rocky ground, ground-contact relationship and directional sand/debris. Do not import its spiked armor, long trailing cloth, anatomy or photorealistic texture.

TWO LOCAL CLOTHING EDITS:
Coordinates refer to IMAGE 1, origin top-left.
A. At x=48.9%, y=53.6%, repair the waist-to-crotch garment construction. Make one coherent waist-fastened short split skirt with a broad FRONT panel and a BACK panel. The front panel must visibly originate from the belt, cover the pelvis continuously, and open naturally over the upper thighs; one continuous finished hem. The back panel visibly originates behind the belt and falls behind the legs. Remove the narrow purple tongue pinched between the thighs, any extra shorts-shaped inner layer and any hem or trim that appears to grow from the bare leg. Maintain modest non-explicit crotch coverage in this low view while retaining exposed upper thighs. Every cloth part has a clear attachment, overlap order and seam. Keep the short silhouette and do not reintroduce long ribbons, cape strips or floating pennants.
B. At x=41.6%, y=33.8%, make the upper garment more designed and attractive. Retain the deep-purple sleeveless silhouette and bare upper arms, but tailor the bodice into a continuous central purple panel framed by TWO broad curved gold-edged seams following the chest and waist. Integrate the existing rounded chest clasp into the collar construction. Add ONE restrained gold embroidered botanical/curved heraldic motif on the upper central panel, and a small cream-colored fabric inset at each side under the arm to distinguish the cut. Use the broad leather belt as the clear join between bodice and skirt. Give the purple cloth soft volume and a few real tension folds; keep its local color continuous. This should read as a coordinated fantasy archer costume with a strong neckline and intentional panel construction, not a plain purple tube dress. Avoid a web of thin straps, cutouts, tiny ornaments, random triangles or spikes.

GROUND AND SIMPLE ENVIRONMENT:
The user now explicitly requests a scene; replace the transparent/gradient background with an opaque, simply organized environment.
Add the same kind of low-angle inclined stony ground as IMAGE 2, with its visible plane sloping from the upper-left toward the lower-right. Align the ground with the target figure's existing feet and perspective instead of changing the body pose. The large near boot at lower right rests or skids firmly against the slope; the smaller rear boot beneath the pelvis also contacts that SAME continuous ground plane. Place tight cast/contact shadows beneath both contact points and let a few foreground dirt clods overlap only the lowest edge of the near boot. This makes her a weight-bearing archer braking in a slide, not floating above a pasted-on floor. Preserve the leg's original screen position and strong near/far scale.
Ground: a few broad weathered stone slab shapes and compacted earth, readable perspective recession, foreground stones larger and softer-edged and far stones smaller and quieter. A small amount of localized cracking, not uniformly fragmented rubble or high-frequency rock grain.
Dynamic dust and stones come from the boots scraping the ground: one low connected sweep of warm dust thrown BACKWARD along the slide path, with a few larger airborne stone fragments close to that wake and fine sand confined near contact. Their motion has one coherent direction. Stronger dust lighting only near the lit edge of the ground wake. Do not spray debris uniformly around the character or create a sandstorm. Keep face, bowstring, fingers, knees and torso readable.
Far environment: muted pale blue-gray open sky and just one or two broad low-contrast distant rock/slope silhouettes. Plenty of quiet space around the face and bow. No detailed castles, miniature towers, speckled clouds, random ruined architecture, floating particles throughout the air or cluttered horizon.

PAINTING AND LIGHT:
Continue IMAGE 1's painted rendering and rich crimson, purple and warm gold palette. The scene and figure must share the existing upper-right warm key light and softer cool ambient shadows. Preserve rounded armor; add no spikes. Ground and dust use the same painted shape language as the character rather than photographic textures. Keep face the focal point and the foreground ground plane subordinate to the archer. Clean character edges, coherent large color areas and limited focused highlights.

One image only, same tall portrait composition, no text, no labels, no comparison panels. OPAQUE BACKGROUND with the simple setting, connected ground and localized dynamic dust described above. Do not reinterpret the figure into a new pose.
